record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a classical multiplier sequence and whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. Equivalently for the multiplier-sequence part, decide whether the real entire function phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} sqrt(k) x^k/(k! k!) belongs to L-P+, the nonnegative-coefficient part of the Laguerre-Polya class. Here a classical multiplier sequence is one whose diagonal operator T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials, and a CZDS is one whose diagonal operator never increases the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial.

evidence.quote: We conjecture that the function phi(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to L - P+.
It is not known whether phi(x) = sum_{k=0}^infinity sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to L - P+.
Problem 39. Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!} is (a) a multiplier sequence (b) a CZDS.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ of real numbers is called a (classical) multiplier sequence if the linear operator $T$ defined on $\mathbb{R}[x]$ by $T[x^k]=\gamma_k x^k$ has the property that, for every real polynomial $p(x)$ with only real zeros, the polynomial $T[p](x)$ also has only real zeros. The sequence is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if, for every real polynomial $p(x)$, the number of nonreal zeros of $T[p](x)$ does not exceed the number of nonreal zeros of $p(x)$.

The Laguerre–Pólya class $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ consists of all entire functions which are locally uniform limits of real polynomials having only real zeros. Equivalently, $f\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ iff $f(z)=cz^m e^{-\alpha z^2+\beta z}\prod_k (1+z/x_k)e^{-z/x_k}$ with $c,\beta,x_k\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\ge 0$, $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, $\sum x_k^{-2}<\infty$. Let $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$ denote the subclass of those $f\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}$ all of whose Taylor coefficients at $0$ are nonnegative.

Consider the sequence
$$\gamma_k=\frac{\sqrt{k}}{k!},\qquad k=0,1,2,\dots,$$
and the associated real entire function
$$\varphi(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\sqrt{k}}{k!\,k!}\,x^k.$$

Decide each of the following:
(a) Is $\{\sqrt{k}/k!\}_{k\ge 0}$ a classical multiplier sequence? Equivalently, does $\varphi(x)$ belong to $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}^+$?
(b) Is $\{\sqrt{k}/k!\}_{k\ge 0}$ a complex zero decreasing sequence?

No source was found establishing or refuting either claim, indicating the problem remains open as posed.
